title: Interactive embedding microburst scratch
content:
Goal:
- Quick exploratory runs to understand latency/queueing behavior for low-latency interactive embedding requests under microburst arrival patterns. Focus: single-vector embed calls (small text payloads), high tail sensitivity, and interaction between batching and autoscaling.

Motivation:
- Product team sees intermittent 150-300ms blips for embeddings in chat UI during bursts. These are small texts (~10-30 tokens).
- Hypothesis: autoscaler warmup + batching heuristics cause transient p95/p99 spikes when burst magnitude crosses a shard boundary. Also possible KV cache or model load contention when multiple small requests hit same GPU host.

Test harness (quick):
- Runner: local replay driver (node) that can emit Poisson + burst waves.
- Model: open-embed/small-1536 (quantized int8 build used in dedicated staging pool).
- Hardware: dedicated-staging-gpu-a100-1 (8x instances), min-replicas 2, scale-to 6, scale-cooldown 30s.
- Batching: adaptive batching on (max_batch 32, timeout 8ms), prefer_latency=true.
- Workload: baseline steady 10 RPS, injection microburst to 200 RPS for 4s every 45s. Payloads: 12 tokens avg.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), cpu/gpu utilization, batch size distribution, queue length, scale events, coldstart counts.

Commands used (notes):
- replay: node tools/replay-driver --pattern microburst --steady 10 --burst 200 --burst-length 4 --cycle 45 --conns 200 --payload sample_small.txt
- monitor: curl http://staging-metrics/api/query?... (prom queries saved in notebook)

Raw quick results (run 2024-11-16 14:00 local):
- Steady-state (no bursts): p50 18ms, p95 36ms, p99 62ms. Avg batch size 1.4 (adaptive kept small)
- During burst first 6s after onset: p50 24ms, p95 140ms, p99 520ms (sharp tail)
- Subsequent cycles (after autoscaler reacted): p50 22ms, p95 48ms, p99 110ms
- Observed scale-up from 2->5 replicas starting ~10s after burst start, finished ~28s.
- Batch size distribution during peak: mode 1, mean 2.6, occasional batches hitting 16 (when queueing allowed).
- GPU utilization: 35% baseline, spiked to 88% on scaled nodes, indicating CPU/GPU mismatch for small payloads.
- Cold model load events: 0 (models preloaded).

Observations / quick hypotheses:
- Tail spikes correlate with two factors: initial queued requests waiting for the batch timeout to collect a larger batch, and the autoscaler reaction delay causing temporary over-subscription on existing nodes (increased queueing).
- Batching heuristics (timeout=8ms) sometimes increases p99 when many connections produce small isolated batches; when requests arrive slightly spaced they get batched causing head-of-line waiting for the batch to fill -> p95 jump.
- When scaled new replicas come online, internal warmup to bring latency back to baseline takes several seconds due to ephemeral scheduler thrash (container init overhead + fast path priming), even though model is hot.

Quick experiments tried (results):
1) Reduce batch timeout to 2ms: p99 reduced from 520ms->220ms in first-cycle, but p50 increased slightly (more small batches). Tradeoff acceptable for interactive use.
2) Aggressive pre-provisioning (min-replicas=4): eliminated the massive p99 spike but increased baseline cost. Best for SLO-critical routes.
3) Enable 'prefer_latency' lane with max_batch=8: smoothed p95/p99 to 90/150ms but reduced throughput headroom.
4) Local request sharding (affinity by tenant -> hashed into per-host queue): showed mixed results; reduced cross-tenant interference but increased imbalance (some hosts hot).

Actionable next steps (short):
- Run controlled A/B with batch-timeout=2ms vs 8ms on a canary route for real traffic (product team signoff). Jira: INC-1327 assigned to me.
- Add a lightweight prime/warmup ping when new replica enters serving pool (small synthetic embed) to reduce priming penalty. Prototype patch in PR linked above.
- Explore a hybrid batching policy: immediate flush for single-client interactive lanes, slightly larger timeout for background/ingestion lanes.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Capture a full flamegraph of queueing path next run (instrument batch path and per-request enqueue timestamps).
- Add histograms for batch assembly latency to telemetry.
- Re-run with different payload lengths (5 token vs 30 token) to confirm token-size sensitivity.
- Share results with product & SRE next sync (cc Marta/Evelyn).

Quick conclusion (draft):
- For interactive embeddings (short texts), tail spikes are mostly driven by batching timeout + scale lag. Lowering the batching timeout for the latency-sensitive lane and modestly increasing min-replicas for that lane reduces p99 dramatically at modest cost. Warmup ping during scale-up also yields measurable improvement.

Raw logs / snippets (copied):
- "[14:02:13] burst start: 200rps, queue len -> 178, mean batch wait 24ms, p99 502ms"
- "[14:02:22] scale event: +3 replicas requested, adding nodes: ok in 26s"

Reference links:

- Related thread: slack://channel/eng-serving-runtime/thread/pt-embed-microburst

End of scratchpad.
